name: Produce the challan a family takes to the bank, printable by the family themselves
priorityReason: Most fees in a Pakistani school are still paid at a bank counter against a printed slip.

goal.capability: to produce the paper slip a family takes to the bank
goal.outcome: a family pays without coming to the school first, and the school gets a stamped copy back it can enter

secondaryActors.involvement: Opens and prints the challan themselves from the app, or collects it from the office.
Configures the challan layout, the bank details and the copy set.

externalActors.involvement: Processes the payment against the printed slip and stamps the copies. Holds no login and receives nothing electronically from this use case.

additional.description: An invoice is issued, and the guardian is sent a link to open and print its challan.

preconditions.condition: An issued, unpaid invoice exists for the student.

establishedBy.name: Issuing fee invoices at different scopes

preconditions.condition: Bank details and the challan layout are configured for the branch.
For an office print, an authenticated session exists.
For a guardian print, the guardian is signed in to the portal and the invoice belongs to their own child.

postConditions: A challan exists as a printable document carrying the amount, the due date and a reference number the bank can quote back.
It is printed in its several identical copies, one for the bank, one for the school and one for the payer.
The guardian has the challan without having come to the school for it.
The reference on the challan ties the eventual bank payment back to the exact invoice, which is what makes the returned school copy enterable.
The invoice is unchanged. Printing a challan is not a payment and moves no money.
Each generation is recorded, so a challan circulating in a family's hands can be traced to when it was produced and by whom.
A challan for a paid or cancelled invoice cannot be produced, so a family cannot be sent to the bank with a slip for a bill that no longer stands.

dataFields.name: Scope
dataFields.validation: One student, a whole class or section, or a whole issue batch — every unpaid invoice raised in one run (BR-4).

dataFields.name: Issue batch
dataFields.validation: The invoice run to print challans for. A batch is exactly one set of invoices, so the period is unambiguous.

dataFields.name: Challan reference
dataFields.validation: Printed on every copy and quoted by the bank. Unique, and it is what ties a bank payment to the invoice (BR-3).

dataFields.name: Amount payable
dataFields.validation: Taken from the invoice. Never typed on the challan (BR-2).

dataFields.name: Due date

dataFields.name: Copies

dataFields.name: Generated by

businessRules.rule: A challan is produced only for an issued, unpaid invoice. A family is never sent to the bank with a slip for a bill that has been paid or cancelled.
Every figure on the challan is taken from the invoice. Nothing on it is typed, so the slip and the ledger cannot disagree.
Every challan carries a unique reference. It is what ties the eventual bank payment back to the exact invoice, and without it a returned school copy cannot be entered with confidence.

A challan covers one invoice. Where a class, section or batch is printed, one challan is produced per unpaid invoice, each with its own reference. Siblings are not combined onto one slip: a single reference must tie the eventual bank payment back to the exact invoice (BR-3), and a slip covering several children returns one stamped copy and one total that cannot be split across their invoices without a guess.
The challan prints in its several identical copies — bank, school and payer — each carrying the same reference and amount.
A guardian prints the challan themselves from the app. They do not have to come to the school to collect it, which is the point of the feature.
Reprinting produces the same challan with the same reference, not a new one. Two references for one bill is how a payment gets entered twice.
Where a late fee policy applies, the amount payable after the due date is printed alongside the amount payable by it, so a family paying late knows what to pay.
Printing a challan moves no money and changes no invoice. It produces a document.
A challan carries no expiry of its own. It becomes unusable when its invoice is paid or cancelled, and the bank copy returned afterwards is what closes it.
Every generation is recorded, so a slip circulating in a family's hands can be traced to when it was produced and by whom.

transitions.condition: The stamped school copy is returned and the payment is entered (UC-04-05).
The invoice amount changes, for example when a late fee accrues, and a fresh challan is produced.
The invoice is cancelled or credited, so the slip no longer represents a debt.

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Fee → Student invoice → Print challan
basicFlow.userAction: Opens an issued unpaid invoice and generates its challan.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Checks the invoice is issued and unpaid, then produces the challan with its reference, amount and due date.
Renders the several identical copies — bank, school and payer — each carrying the same reference and amount.

basicFlow.navigation: Portal → My children's fees → Print challan
basicFlow.userAction: Opens the challan and prints it at home, rather than collecting it from the office.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Produces the same challan with the same reference, for their own child's invoice only.

basicFlow.navigation: Takes the printed slip to the bank
basicFlow.userAction: Pays the challan at the bank counter.
Stamps all copies and keeps the bank copy.

basicFlow.navigation: Returns the stamped school copy to the office

basicFlow.userAction: Enters the payment from the stamped school copy, quoting the challan reference.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Matches the reference to the invoice and records the payment there.

alternateFlows.condition: A whole issue batch needs printing at once
alternateFlows.navigation: Fee → Bulk challan printing → Select batch
alternateFlows.behaviour: One challan is produced per unpaid invoice in the batch, each with its own reference, and they print together. A batch is one issue run, so the billing period is unambiguous.

alternateFlows.condition: A whole class needs printing at once
alternateFlows.behaviour: Challans are generated for every unpaid invoice in the class or section and printed as a batch.

alternateFlows.condition: The guardian asks the office for the slip instead
alternateFlows.behaviour: The office prints and hands it over. It is the same challan with the same reference (BR-7).

alternateFlows.condition: The guardian wants it sent rather than printed
alternateFlows.behaviour: The challan is sent to the guardian's contact and the send is logged against the invoice.

alternateFlows.condition: A late fee has accrued since the challan was printed
alternateFlows.behaviour: The earlier challan is superseded and a fresh one is produced for the higher amount, so the bank is not given a slip for a figure that no longer matches the ledger (BR-8).

departures.requirement: The printed slip matches the bank's expected layout exactly, since a bank clerk rejects a slip that does not.
A batch of 500 challans is generated within 60 seconds and produced as one printable document.
Reprinting produces the same reference. Two references for one bill is how a payment gets entered twice.

openQuestions.question: How many copies does the school's bank require, and what are they called?
openQuestions.assumption: Three — bank, school and payer. Confirm with the bank.

openQuestions.question: Does the bank require a particular challan layout or barcode?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified, and a bank clerk will reject a slip that does not match.

openQuestions.question: Siblings can no longer be combined onto one challan, because one reference must tie a bank payment to one invoice. Should a household instead be billed on a single consolidated invoice at issue time, so one payment settles all its children?
openQuestions.assumption: No consolidation at launch. Each child is billed and pays separately.

openQuestions.question: What happens when a family pays an old challan after a late fee has accrued?
openQuestions.assumption: The shortfall stays outstanding. Not specified.

openQuestions.question: Can a guardian print a challan for an invoice that is already overdue?
openQuestions.assumption: Yes, showing the amount payable after the due date.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: academic-session-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every academic record carries an academic session ID. Lists default to the current open session.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: money
conventionsApplied.rule: All monetary values are stored as fixed-point decimals in the smallest currency unit, never as floating point. Displayed as PKR with a thousands separator and two decimal places. Rounding is half-up at the line.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: bulk-actions
conventionsApplied.rule: Any bulk operation reports a per-row result, commits valid rows and lists rejected rows with the reason. A bulk action never fails as a whole because of one bad row.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
